drafted_from: workflow:check-my-code-against-my-rules's own file, tools/workflows/recipes/check-my-code-against-my-rules.json (its wake, definition and steps), and tool:check-an-archive-against-my-rules.
start_here: Say to your AI: "Check these repositories against my rules every hour." The AI turns on workflow:check-my-code-against-my-rules's wake hourly with checks, one per repository (its archive address and your rules), as the switch's input. Each hour each newest commit is checked, and you are told only about a repository that breaks a rule.
no_lists_because: It keeps nothing: the repositories, their rules and recorded findings are the switch's input, and a check that finds something tells one notice.
instructions: 1. Turn on this workflow's wake hourly once, with store (where the person keeps their notices, its language and its login's vault name) and checks: one item per repository, each {archive (the https address of the repository's archive, such as its host's archive of a branch), rules, recorded when some findings are already written down}. A wake has one switch, so to add a repository switch it on again with every check, the new one included.

2. To catch callers of names another repository retired, add subjects_from to a check: was (that repository's archive at the older commit), now (its archive today), path_matches, pattern and capture naming where and how a name is declared; a rule then collects from that subject by name.
3. Read each notice that comes: its body counts the findings; a finding whose name has a recorded new home says where it moved.

rules.why: A retirement is done only when every caller has moved.
